reasoning_traces.think:
Spearman’s framework partitions psychology into formative and individual layers. Formative psychology (lower) reflects structural emergence from hereditary (H) and training (T), modeled as static input layers. Individual psychology (upper) encodes dynamic cognitive traits (s, c, o, w, g) derived from H and T. Normative mental events (M) evolve as a temporal sequence governed by these latent factors. The system exhibits duality: H/T → structure (formative) vs. s/c/o/w/g → behavior (individual). Failure modes include misalignment between H/T and s/c/o/w/g, leading to inconsistent mental event sequences. The mathematical structure supports Bayesian updating of H/T priors against observed M sequences, enabling predictive inference.
